contexts.description: Full-stack ability and GAS (Gameplay Ability System) design suite: authors ability specs, computes balance formulas, generates GAS C++ code, and validates tags. The forge sub-system lets designers tune attribute weights interactively. Cross-references the character blueprint to keep ability tags in sync with the UE5 project.
contexts.name: ability-design

contexts.description: Animation video generation pipeline using Leonardo Hailuo for text-to-video and image-to-video. The anim-critique module applies a VLM aesthetic ruler to multi-frame filmstrips scoring six dimensions (anticipation, weight, timing, follow-through, silhouette, believability) and returning a topFix suggestion. This closes the loop on animation quality without human review for every iteration.
contexts.name: anim-video-gen

contexts.description: Animation pipeline tools covering retargeting from Mixamo/MHA sources to UE5 Manny, state graph authoring, combo/montage sequencing, and runtime budget tracking. The anim-critique tier applies a VLM aesthetic ruler to multi-frame filmstrips scoring anticipation, weight, timing, follow-through, silhouette, and believability. Integrates with the harness for closed-loop code-authored animation via numeric FK feedback.
contexts.name: animation-module

contexts.description: Next.js App Router shell with tab-based navigation between module domains. The LRU module cache suspends hidden modules to pause their timers and subscriptions. useSuspendableEffect and useSuspendableSelector are the standard hooks for suspension-aware work. The app shell tracks hydration state to gate portals and document access, preventing SSR/client mismatches.
contexts.name: app-navigation

contexts.description: Audio scene management, asset library, and AI voice/SFX/music generation. Supports spatial audio design with scene-viewport tools, voice activity detection, and ElevenLabs integration via a provider mesh. Assets are persisted with content-hash deduplication and can be wired to Unreal audio events.
contexts.name: audio-module

contexts.description: Blender MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration enabling direct Blender scripting from the app via a TCP bridge. Supports mesh generation, material application, and pipeline export to UE5 formats. The 3D studio components provide an in-browser WebGL/Three.js preview of generated assets. Guided setup walks users through the Blender connection.
contexts.name: blender-3d-integration

contexts.description: Blueprint transpilation suite that parses UE5 Blueprint JSON exports into a semantic AST, diffs them structurally, and generates equivalent C++ with a Shiki-highlighted code viewer. A jargon/glossary system explains Blueprint nodes in plain language. Supports round-trip C++ → Blueprint import back into UE5 via the bridge.
contexts.name: blueprint-tools

contexts.description: End-to-end UE5 build and packaging pipeline covering preflight checks, cook, smoke tests, and size-budget enforcement. A scheduled nightly build runs via the server-side cron in instrumentation.ts, skipping unchanged git HEADs. Exposes a multi-step wizard UI for manual build initiation and surfaces cook progress with phase segmentation.
contexts.name: build-packaging

contexts.description: The main LayoutLab interface that serves as the application homepage, providing a Category → Catalog → Entity tree with a Baseline view for pipeline step navigation. A compact bridge strip shows live UE5 connection status. Responsive shell collapses to drawer panels below 1100px. Hydrates pipeline artifact state from the server on entity-open and renders a config-complete summary in the pipeline header.
contexts.name: catalog-browser-ui

contexts.description: SQLite persistence layer for catalog entities, pipeline artifacts, and the canon (authoritative data set). Exposes REST API routes for reading/writing pipeline artifacts, and a drain endpoint that flips deferred L3/L4 artifacts to pass/fail after live UE5 verification. The labArtifactClient on the frontend wraps these endpoints and merges server state into the client pipeline store.
contexts.name: catalog-database

contexts.description: Claude Code CLI integration that spawns a CLI subprocess, parses stream-JSON output with session management, and wires domain-specific skills knowledge packs. The task system uses @@CALLBACK markers so Claude's output is intercepted, validated as JSON, and POSTed back to the app's API. The useModuleCLI hook is the standard way for module components to launch and track CLI sessions.
contexts.name: cli-terminal-system

contexts.description: Crash report ingestion and analysis engine that parses UE5 crash logs, maps call stacks to known patterns via a glossary, and suggests fixes. The bridge-doctor component diagnoses live connection failures between the app and UE5. Integrates with the game director to surface crash regressions across sessions.
contexts.name: crash-analysis

contexts.description: Single SQLite instance at ~/.pof/pof.db shared across all subsystems via better-sqlite3 in WAL mode. The db.ts module manages the connection lifecycle, migrations, and shared utilities. Each feature domain has its own *-db.ts file with typed query functions. next.config.ts externalizes better-sqlite3 to prevent bundling on the server.
contexts.name: database-layer

contexts.description: Tracks the implementation status of every game feature across all modules in a visual matrix view, powered by a SQLite backing store. The Feature Constellation renders a layered tech-tree dependency graph for a single module with status-colored nodes and a recommended-next pulse. The NBA engine reads these statuses to suggest the highest-value next action.
contexts.name: feature-matrix-tracking

contexts.description: Session-level project health tracking that aggregates build quality scores, regression signals, and crash trends across development sessions. The severity legend surfaces critical findings with one-click fix suggestions. Provides a regression tracker that diffs session vs session to catch newly introduced issues. Depends on the evaluator for per-module scores and crash analyzer for fault signals.
contexts.name: game-director-system

contexts.description: Game Design Document tooling that validates implementation against a structured GDD, synthesizes design documents from game metadata, and renders the GDD as an interactive Mermaid architecture diagram with clickable nodes that jump to the relevant module. The GDD pitch tool generates investor/producer-ready summaries. Depends on module navigation to wire diagram clicks to the workspace.
contexts.name: gdd-compliance

contexts.description: Autonomous development harness that orchestrates multi-step game feature builds end-to-end: authoring spec, generating C++, submitting to UE5 via the bridge, running tests, and verifying via visual capture. The pof-mcp stdio server exposes harness capabilities to Claude Code CLI as MCP tools, enabling fully autonomous iteration loops from the terminal.
contexts.name: harness-autonomy

contexts.description: AI image generation pipeline supporting Leonardo.ai (2D tiling/transparency/ControlNet/upscaler) and other providers. Every generation downloads then deletes the asset from the provider. Supports genome build codes for sharing generation parameters via deflate+base64url. The one-shot lab enables rapid single-image generation with style direction.
contexts.name: image-generation

contexts.description: The reference implementation of the catalog pipeline for the Items catalog (13 steps: economy, art, attributes, etc.). Serves as the canonical example of how every catalog pipeline should be built using CliProduce + StepFrame + CandidateGallery. Tests serve as the regression guard for the pipeline authoring conventions.
contexts.name: item-catalog-pipeline

contexts.description: Domain knowledge base that powers the skills system injected into CLI sessions. Contains structured knowledge about UE5 assets, gotchas, patterns, and best practices. The implementation planner uses this knowledge to generate step-by-step build plans. The localization system provides i18n knowledge for UE5 content pipelines.
contexts.name: knowledge-system

contexts.description: Procedural level generation tools that let designers describe a world in plain language and receive a scatter/placement plan. Supports zone graph generation, PCG (Procedural Content Generation) integration, and a live in-browser procgen preview. The text-to-world flow converts narrative descriptions into actionable UE5 PCG parameters.
contexts.name: level-design-module

contexts.description: PBR material and texture pipeline tools for UE5 Substrate materials. Supports one-prompt material generation, interactive PBR preview sphere, and channel-packing for UE5 texture sets. Integrates with the catalog pipeline for material acceptance validation.
contexts.name: material-module

contexts.description: Four-pass quality evaluation system (structure → quality → performance → compliance) that runs automated assessments against each module's code. Deep eval runs multi-dimensional scoring in parallel across configurable prompts. The evaluator module renders scorecards, trend charts, and drill-down views per evaluation pass. Results drive the Game Director's quality regression tracking.
contexts.name: module-evaluator

contexts.description: Defines the core module registry that organizes the game development workspace into domain-specific modules (combat, animation, loot, etc.) each with checklists, quick actions, and knowledge tips. The registry drives what checklist items, prompts, and NBA (Next Best Action) recommendations appear in the UI. Depends on feature-definitions for the dependency graph that powers cross-module navigation.
contexts.name: module-system

contexts.description: Test gate runner that executes L3/L4 pipeline acceptance gates against the live UE5 editor via pluggable executors (bridge/spawn/visual). The drain API flips deferred artifacts to pass/fail after verification. The observation spine defines typed contracts for what can be measured (position, animation-state, health, damage, timing). Visual capture feeds frames to the VLM critique gate.
contexts.name: observation-testing

contexts.description: Acceptance logic engine that derives L0–L4 tier status (data/human-selection/static/runtime/visual) from pipeline artifact state rather than manual toggles. Resolves config-complete vs deferred status, provides the language/labels used in acceptance banners, and summarizes entity pipeline health. The acceptance engine is the single source of truth for whether a pipeline step has been completed.
contexts.name: pipeline-acceptance-engine

contexts.description: Shared component library for catalog pipeline steps implementing the View/Produce/Acceptance model. CliProduce handles CLI invocation with direction text and prompt logic; StepFrame wraps steps with an acceptance banner; ChartPanel renders budget bars, scatter, and histograms; CandidateGallery browses and compares generative batches. Every pipeline step must reuse these rather than hand-rolling equivalent UI.
contexts.name: pipeline-step-components

contexts.description: Composable prompt construction system that injects UE5 project context into AI prompts for each module checklist item. A fluent builder assembles prompts across six sections (Project Context → Domain Context → Task Instructions → Best Practices → Output Schema → Success Criteria), with per-module specializations and a prompt evolution system that tracks versions and diffs. Central to the entire app's value proposition of generating UE5-specific code guidance.
contexts.name: prompt-engineering

contexts.description: Interactive combat and economy simulation environments that let designers validate balance without running UE5. The combat simulator models damage pipelines, dodge chains, and hit reactions with real-time parameter tuning. The economy simulator runs sensitivity sweeps on loot distribution and faucet/sink tables. Both export validated configs back to the catalog pipeline.
contexts.name: simulation-tools

contexts.description: 37 Zustand stores with persist middleware providing centralized state for every feature domain. Transient runtime fields are excluded from persistence to prevent snapshot instability on rehydration. The ProjectModuleBridge service breaks the circular dependency between project and module stores. The event bus provides typed pub/sub with a replay buffer for cross-store communication.
contexts.name: state-management

contexts.description: Dual-bridge communication layer to UE5: the mcp-unreal bridge (port 8090) for general editor commands and the PoF Bridge plugin (port 30040) for game-specific automation including run-automation, snapshot capture, and manifest queries. The pofBridgeStore tracks connection health; the ue5BridgeStore tracks build/compile status. Used by every subsystem that needs to verify state in the running UE5 editor.
contexts.name: ue5-bridge-client

contexts.description: Scenario harness for running controlled experiments in UE5: authoring scenario JSON, submitting to the PoF Bridge's inbox, reading captured observation frames, and comparing results across configurations. The Observation Spine (SP1) defines five observation verbs (position, animation state, health, etc.) with typed contracts verified by 21 tests. The reality ledger reconciles referenced vs existing vs valid vs runtime assets.
contexts.name: ue5-experiment-runner

contexts.description: Shared design-system component library enforcing consistent tokens: accessible modals with focus traps, animated tab bars, slider primitives, MeterBar/ProgressRing/ScoreRing, MicroLabel, RarityBadge, InlineErrorRetry, ChartLegend, StatusTag, and focus-ring tokens. ESLint rules enforce no raw hex colors (use chart-colors), no console.* (use logger), and dynamic Tailwind classes must use inline styles.
contexts.name: ui-primitives
